# Load packages

Install the necessary packages for our analysis.  The function 'require' returns a true value if it is already installed, so if it is not, we need to install before loading

```{r Packages, warning=FALSE}

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(fgsea)
library(reshape2)
library(msigdbr)
library(stringr)

library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(pheatmap)

library(clusterProfiler)
library(enrichplot)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
library(AnnotationDbi)

library(UpSetR)

library(corrplot)

library(BiocParallel)

library(e1071) # For skewness calculation
```

# Set working directory

Your working directory is where all your output files are going to be saved.

``` {r WorkingDirectory, tidy=TRUE, tidy.opts=list(width.cutoff=60)}
# you will need to change this to the directory you are working in
# make sure to include the / at the end of the directory path

input_directory = "C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/"

male_normhyp_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,"dream_diffexpr_male_hypnorm_batchcorr.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
female_normhyp_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,"dream_diffexpr_female_hypnorm_batchcorr.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
# correct sign to reflect hyp:norm
male_normhyp_data$logFC = -1 * male_normhyp_data$logFC
male_normhyp_data$t = -1 * male_normhyp_data$t
male_normhyp_data$z.std = -1 * male_normhyp_data$z.std
female_normhyp_data$logFC = -1 * female_normhyp_data$logFC
female_normhyp_data$t = -1 * female_normhyp_data$t
female_normhyp_data$z.std = -1 * female_normhyp_data$z.std

norm_femalemale_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,"dream_diffexpr_norm_femalemale_batchcorr.csv"), check.names = FALSE)
hyp_femalemale_data = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,"dream_diffexpr_hyp_femalemale_batchcorr.csv"), check.names = FALSE)


```

# compare male to female in norm vs hyp

```{r}

# ------- hyp diff in male vs female -------

merged_data = merge(male_normhyp_data, female_normhyp_data, by = "genes")
merged_data = merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "both_sig",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "both_nom_sig",
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y >= 0.05 ~ "sig_male",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y >= 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_male",
      adj.P.Val.x >= 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "sig_female",
      P.Value.x >= 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_female",
      TRUE       ~ "not"
    )
  )
merged_data_label = merged_data %>%
  group_by(sig) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(logFC.x), n = 15, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = logFC.x, y = logFC.y, color = sig, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_point() +
  #scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "sig_male" = "blue","sig_female" = "orange", "not" = "grey")) +
  #scale_alpha_manual(values = c("both_sig" = 0.9, "sig_male" = 0.9,"sig_female" = 0.9, "not" = 0.3)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "both_nom_sig" = "pink", "sig_male" = "blue", "nom_sig_male" = "lightblue", "sig_female" = "orange", "nom_sig_female" = "khaki1", "not" = "grey")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("both_sig" = 0.9, "both_nom_sig" = 0.7, "sig_male" = 0.9, "nom_sig_male" = 0.7, "sig_female" = 0.9, "nom_sig_female" = 0.7, "not" = 0.3)) +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = merged_data_label,
    aes(label = genes),
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave(paste0(input_directory, "scatter_malehyp_femalehyp.pdf"))


# ------- sex diff in norm vs hyp -------

merged_data = merge(norm_femalemale_data, hyp_femalemale_data, by = "genes")
merged_data = merged_data %>%
  mutate(
    sig = case_when(
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "both_sig",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "both_nom_sig",
      adj.P.Val.x < 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y >= 0.05 ~ "sig_norm",
      P.Value.x < 0.05 & P.Value.y >= 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_norm",
      adj.P.Val.x >= 0.05 & adj.P.Val.y < 0.05 ~ "sig_hyp",
      P.Value.x >= 0.05 & P.Value.y < 0.05 ~ "nom_sig_hyp",
      TRUE       ~ "not"
    )
  )

merged_data_label = merged_data %>%
  group_by(sig) %>%
  slice_max(order_by = abs(logFC.x), n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = logFC.x, y = logFC.y, color = sig, alpha = sig)) +
  geom_point() +
  #xlim(-5,5) +
  #ylim(-5,5)  +
  #scale_color_manual(values = c("both_sig" = "red", "sig_norm" = "green","sig_hyp" = "purple", "not" = "grey")) +
```

# GSEA 

```{r gsea}

datasets = list("norm_femalemale" = data.frame(norm_femalemale_data), "hyp_femalemale" = data.frame(hyp_femalemale_data), "male_normhyp" = data.frame(male_normhyp_data), "female_normhyp" = data.frame(female_normhyp_data))

sig_pathways_list = list()

for (name in names(datasets)) {

  print (name)
  
  dataset = datasets[[name]]
  
  # Create ranked vector
  # Common choice: moderated t-statistic
  ranks = dataset$t
  
  # Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
  names(ranks) = dataset$genes
  
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  ranks = ranks[!is.na(ranks)]
  ranks = sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # Get Hallmark pathways from MSigDB
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")
  msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "HPO")
  
  pathways = split(msig$gene_symbol, msig$gs_name)
  
  # Run fgsea
  suppressWarnings({
    fgseaRes = fgsea(
      pathways = pathways,
      stats = ranks,
      minSize = 15,
      maxSize = 500,
      BPPARAM = SerialParam()
    )
  })
  
  # Sort by significance
  fgseaRes = fgseaRes[order(fgseaRes$padj), ]
  
  # write out results
  fgseaRes_out = as.data.frame(fgseaRes)
  fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge = sapply(fgseaRes_out$leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ",")
  #write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(input_directory,"t_fgsea_H_results_", name, ".csv"))
  #write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(input_directory,"t_fgsea_GOBP_results_", name, ".csv"))
  #write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(input_directory,"t_fgsea_KEGG_results_", name, ".csv"))
  write.csv(fgseaRes_out, file = paste0(input_directory,"t_fgsea_HPO_results_", name, ".csv"))
  
  padj_threshold = 0.01 # 0.05 for H, 0.001 for GO BP, 0.01 for KEGG
  
  # save sig pathways
  sig_pathways_list[[name]] = fgseaRes$pathway[fgseaRes$padj < padj_threshold]
  
  # plot bubble plot
  plot_df = as.data.frame(fgseaRes) %>%
  filter(padj < padj_threshold)

  bubble_plot = ggplot(plot_df,
         aes(x = NES,
             y = reorder(pathway, NES),
             size = size,
             color = -log10(padj))) +
    geom_point() +
    ggtitle(name) +
    theme_bw()
  print(bubble_plot)
  ggsave(plot = bubble_plot, filename = paste0(input_directory,"t_fgsea_HPO_bubbleplot_", name, ".pdf"), height = 8, width = 8)

}
```


# clusterProfiler

```{r clusterprofiler, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

for (name in names(datasets)) {

  dataset = datasets[[name]]
  
  # Create ranked vector
  # Common choice: moderated t-statistic
  ranks = dataset$t
  
  # Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
  names(ranks) = dataset$genes
  
  # Remove duplicates and NAs
  ranks = ranks[!is.na(ranks)]
  ranks = sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # Get Hallmark pathways from MSigDB
  msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
  #msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")
  
  term2gene = msig[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")]
  
  gse = GSEA(
    geneList = ranks,
    TERM2GENE = term2gene,
    by = "fgsea",
    pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
    minGSSize = 15,
    maxGSSize = 500,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
  
  gse = pairwise_termsim(gse, method = "JC")
  
  # plot only significant categories
  sig_terms = as.data.frame(gse)$ID[as.data.frame(gse)$p.adjust < 0.05]
  if(length(sig_terms > 0)) {
    ep = emapplot(
      gse,
      showCategory = sig_terms,
      layout = "kk",
      color = "p.adjust"
    )
    print(ep)
  }
  
  sig_terms = as.data.frame(gse)$ID[as.data.frame(gse)$p.adjust < 0.01]
  if(length(sig_terms) > 0) {
    cp = cnetplot(
      gse,
      showCategory = sig_terms
    )
    print (cp)
  }
}

```

# variance gsea

```{r var_gsea}

var_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/variance_with_means.csv")

test_columns = c("AvgVariance_male_norm", "AvgVariance_male_hyp", "AvgVariance_fem_norm", "AvgVariance_fem_hyp")

# correlation matrix of variation
var_data_filter = var_data[, colnames(var_data) %in% test_columns]
rownames(var_data_filter) = var_data$Geneid

cor_mat = cor(var_data_filter,
               method = "pearson",
               use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

corrplot(
  cor_mat,
  method = "color",
  type = "upper",
  order = "hclust",
  addCoef.col = "black",
  tl.col = "black",
  tl.srt = 45,
  diag = FALSE,
  col = colorRampPalette(
    c("blue", "white", "red")
  )(200)
)

# gsea

# since variance in gene expression is well correlated across sample groups,
#   run gsea on average
ranks = rowMeans(var_data[, colnames(var_data) %in% c("AvgVariance_fem_hyp", "AvgVariance_fem_norm", "AvgVariance_male_norm", "AvgVariance_male_hyp")])

# Names must be gene symbols (or whatever ID matches pathway genes)
names(ranks) = var_data$Geneid

# Remove duplicates and NAs
ranks = ranks[!is.na(ranks)]
ranks = sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)

# Get Hallmark pathways from MSigDB
msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens",collection = "H")
#msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
#msig = msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "C2", subcollection = "CP:KEGG_LEGACY")

term2gene = msig[, c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")]

gse = GSEA(
  geneList = ranks,
  TERM2GENE = term2gene,
  by = "fgsea",
  pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
  minGSSize = 15,
  maxGSSize = 500,
  verbose = FALSE, 
  scoreType = "pos"
)

write.csv(gse@result, file = paste0(input_directory,"gsea_H_AvgVar_results.csv"))

plot_df = as.data.frame(gse@result) %>%
  filter(qvalue < 0.05) # 0.05 for H, 0.001 for GO BP
  
bubble_plot = ggplot(plot_df,
       aes(x = NES,
           y = reorder(ID, NES),
           size = setSize,
           color = -log10(qvalue))) +
  geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("Average Variance") +
  theme_bw()
print(bubble_plot)

gse = pairwise_termsim(gse, method = "JC")

# plot only significant categories
sig_terms = as.data.frame(gse)$ID[as.data.frame(gse)$p.adjust < 0.05]
if(length(sig_terms > 0)) {
  ep = emapplot(
    gse,
    showCategory = sig_terms,
    layout = "kk",
    color = "p.adjust"
  ) + 
    ggtitle("Avg Variance")
  print(ep)
}
```

# Using different measure of variance

```{r}

# load data
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data = read.csv("C:/Users/plaisiersb/OneDrive - National Institutes of Health/Documents/Projects/Placenta/HG38/Correct_BatchCovariate/lcpm_norm_batchcorrected.csv")
rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data) = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data$gene
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data$gene = NULL

pheno = data.frame(colnames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)[-1])
colnames(pheno) = c("sample")
pheno$sex = ifelse(grepl("XY",pheno$sample, fixed = TRUE),"male","female")
pheno$status = ifelse(grepl("Cont",pheno$sample, fixed = TRUE),"normotensive","hypertensive")
pheno$placenta = str_split(pheno$sample, "_", simplify = TRUE)[, 1]
pheno$quadrant = str_split(pheno$sample, "_", simplify = TRUE)[, 2]
pheno$sex_status = paste0(pheno$sex, "_", pheno$status)

# create placenta level pheno file for merging later
pheno_placenta = pheno
pheno_placenta$sample = NULL
pheno_placenta$quadrant = NULL
pheno_placenta = pheno_placenta[!duplicated(pheno_placenta$placenta), ]

# Ensure pheno matches expression matrix
lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data[,pheno$sample]
stopifnot(all(pheno$sample == colnames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)))


placentas = unique(pheno$placenta)

residual_var_list = list()

for(placenta in placentas){

    placenta_samples = pheno$sample[
        pheno$placenta == placenta
    ]

    expr_placenta = lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data[, placenta_samples, drop = FALSE]

    # Mean expression per gene
    gene_mean = rowMeans(expr_placenta)

    # Variance across individuals
    gene_var = apply(expr_placenta, 1, var)

    # Avoid log(0)
    gene_var[gene_var <= 0] = min(
        gene_var[gene_var > 0]
    ) / 2

    # Fit mean-variance trend
    fit = loess(
        log10(gene_var) ~ gene_mean,
        span = 0.5
    )

    # Residual variability
    resid_var = residuals(fit)

    residual_var_list[[placenta]] = data.frame(
        gene = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data),
        mean_logCPM = gene_mean,
        variance = gene_var,
        residual_variability = resid_var
    )
}

residual_var_mat = do.call(
    cbind,
    lapply(
        residual_var_list,
        function(x) x$residual_variability
    )
)

rownames(residual_var_mat) = rownames(lcpm_norm_batchcorrect_data)

# grab high variance genes 
high_var_genes = lapply(
  residual_var_list,
  function(df) {
    df$gene[df$residual_variability > 1]
  }
)

# tally genes identified as variable

# Combine all genes from all tissues
all_genes = unlist(high_var_genes)

# Count occurrences

# Convert to data frame

  gene = names(gene_counts),
  n_tissues = as.integer(gene_counts),
  row.names = NULL
)

# Sort by number of tissues
gene_count_df = gene_count_df[
  order(gene_count_df$n_tissues, decreasing = TRUE),
]

# plot genes with high residual variation and high expression
var_data$AveExp = rowMeans(var_data[,grepl("AveExpr_",colnames(var_data))])
gene_count_df$AveExpr = var_data$AveExp[match(gene_count_df$gene,var_data$Geneid)]
```

# Compare 3 enrichment results

For all three GSEA runs (H, GO BP, KEGG), for each sex (hypnorm), print all results that are significant in that sex (adjp < 0.05), but definitely not in the other (adjp > 0.5).  

```{r}

male_profile_files = c("t_fgsea_KEGG_results_male_normhyp.csv", "t_fgsea_GOBP_results_male_normhyp.csv", "t_fgsea_H_results_male_normhyp.csv")

female_profile_files = c("t_fgsea_KEGG_results_female_normhyp.csv", "t_fgsea_GOBP_results_female_normhyp.csv", "t_fgsea_H_results_female_normhyp.csv")

results1 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,male_profile_files[1]))
results2 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,male_profile_files[2]))
results3 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,male_profile_files[3]))
male_results = rbind(results1, results2, results3)

results1 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,female_profile_files[1]))
results2 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,female_profile_files[2]))
results3 = read.csv(paste0(input_directory,female_profile_files[3]))
female_results = rbind(results1, results2, results3)

merge_results = merge(male_results, female_results, by = "pathway", suffixes = c("_male", "_fem"))

# filters
pval_threshold = 0.05
merge_results_filtered = merge_results[merge_results$padj_male < pval_threshold | merge_results$padj_fem < pval_threshold, ]

male_specific = na.omit(merge_results_filtered[merge_results_filtered$padj_male < pval_threshold & merge_results_filtered$padj_fem > 0.5,])

male_specific_up = na.omit(male_specific[male_specific$NES_male > 0,])
male_specific_down = na.omit(male_specific[male_specific$NES_male < 0,])

female_specific = na.omit(merge_results_filtered[merge_results_filtered$padj_male > 0.5 & merge_results_filtered$padj_fem < pval_threshold,])

female_specific_up = na.omit(female_specific[female_specific$NES_fem > 0,])
female_specific_down = na.omit(female_specific[female_specific$NES_fem < 0,])

both_sig = na.omit(merge_results_filtered[merge_results_filtered$padj_male < pval_threshold & merge_results_filtered$padj_fem < pval_threshold,])

both_sig_up = both_sig[both_sig$NES_male > 0 & both_sig$NES_fem > 0,]
both_sig_down = both_sig[both_sig$NES_male < 0 & both_sig$NES_fem < 0,]

list_of_profiles = list("male_specific_up" = male_specific_up, 
                        "male_specific_down" = male_specific_down, 
                        "female_specific_up" = female_specific_up,
                        "both_sig_up" = both_sig_up,
                        "both_sig_down" = both_sig_down)

for (profile in names(list_of_profiles)) {
  # similarity tree
  
  enr_data = list_of_profiles[[profile]]
  
  if(grepl("female", profile, fixed = TRUE)) {
    leading_edge_list = setNames(
      strsplit(enr_data$leadingEdge_fem, ","),
      enr_data$pathway
    )
  } else {
    leading_edge_list = setNames(
      strsplit(enr_data$leadingEdge_male, ","),
      enr_data$pathway
    )
  }
  
  # remove any leading/trailing whitespace
  leading_edge_list = lapply(
    leading_edge_list,
    trimws
  )
  
  # calculate overlap similarity matrix
  jaccard = function(x, y) {
    length(intersect(x, y)) / length(union(x, y))
  }
  
  pathways = names(leading_edge_list)
  
  sim_mat = outer(
    pathways, pathways,
    Vectorize(function(a, b) {
      jaccard(leading_edge_list[[a]], leading_edge_list[[b]])
    })
  )
  
  rownames(sim_mat) = pathways
  colnames(sim_mat) = pathways
    
  # turn similarity into distance and cluster
  dist_mat = as.dist(1 - sim_mat)
  hc = hclust(dist_mat, method = "average")
  
  # plot dendrogram
  pdf(
    paste0(input_directory,"pathway_dendrogram_",profile,".pdf"),
    width = 30,
    height = 10
  )
  
  plot (hc, cex = 0.4)
  
  dev.off()

}
```
